lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! Let's look at node images: the official ones, and your own.
Your test cluster should run the same Slurm release as your site. So which node image do you pick, and when do you build your own?
There's one official node image per Slurm release line that sind supports.
Latest is the newest line. A year and month tag tracks the newest patch of that line, and a full version pins just one.
To run a cluster on one release line, set its image under defaults in the cluster configuration.
But every tag can move when the images are rebuilt. For reproducible CI, pin one exact build by its sha two fifty-six instead.
Every official image is based on Rocky Linux. It builds Slurm and a full MPI stack from source, and runs systemd as init.
Each published image is attested, so the GitHub CLI can check that the sind image workflow built it.
You only build locally when you change the Dockerfile. make image builds every release line, and bake can build just one.
Building your own image? It must boot systemd as init, with the SSH daemon and munge enabled.
Install the Slurm daemons without enabling them. sind enables each by role, when all nodes are ready.
So: pick a release line by its tag, pin one exact build for CI, and give your own image systemd, sshd and munge.
Next up: containers that exit with code two fifty-five. See you there!
